title: Knowledge check: Setting Up the jQuery Development Environment

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of setting up the jquery development environment?
options: Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.
Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
A page must load one compatible jQuery build before dependent application code runs. Keep the chosen version explicit and verify the loaded file in the browser Network and Console panels.
questions.answer_key: A page must load one compatible jQuery build before dependent application code runs. Keep the chosen version explicit and verify the loaded file in the browser Network and Console panels.
questions.explanation: A page must load one compatible jQuery build before dependent application code runs. Keep the chosen version explicit and verify the loaded file in the browser Network and Console panels. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying preparing an html, css, and javascript project?
options: Use preparing an html, css, and javascript project deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Use preparing an html, css, and javascript project deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with setting up the jquery development environment?
options: Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
